subject: Dedicated Pool Commitment — SKU prioritization matrix & throughput checkpoints

Subject: RFI: Dedicated capacity sizing and SKU fit (Novacorp)

Kimberly —

Thanks for taking this RFI. We're consolidating our inference workloads and put together a formal questionnaire for committed capacity sizing. High level asks below; full spreadsheet attached. We need:

- Expected throughput targets (tokens/sec and p95 tail) per workload class (interactive chat, batch embed, reranking)
- Recommended GPU SKU mix for a staged commitment (pilot -> 6mo -> steady state) including fallback lanes when primary SKUs are constrained
- Latency and throughput trade-offs with quantized variants (4-bit/8-bit) and expected cost delta per 1M tokens
- Any minimum commitment term and proposed termination/overage policies
- Timeline for procurement & onboarding (PoC -> reserved pool -> production)

Attached: Novacorp_RFI_questionnaire.xlsx (we populated workload names and peak QPS). Would appreciate a workbook-level answer with numbers we can plug into our procurement model.

Can you confirm you can deliver a completed sizing workbook by the end of week? Also please flag any assumptions you need from our side.

Regards,

Anya Petrov

Novacorp Technologies

Subject: Re: RFI: Dedicated capacity sizing and SKU fit (Novacorp)

Anya —

Thanks for the detailed questionnaire and the populated workload sheet. We're able to deliver a completed sizing workbook but want to align on a couple of assumptions before we finalize numbers:

1) Sequence-length profiles: you provided median/peak tokens but not tail token length distribution. For cost-fit, we need 50th/90th/99th percentile seq len per workload. Can you confirm or we will assume 1/8/16k distribution for interactive chat?

2) Acceptable tail-latency SLOs: is p95=150ms and p99=350ms acceptable for interactive? If you need stricter p99 we should size more conservative SKUs or add reserved headroom.

3) Quantization acceptance: Are we allowed to propose GPT-style 4-bit quantized variants for non-sensitive workloads (embeddings, rerank) or does Novacorp require FP16 across the board?

Plan: we'll draft a workbook that includes three commitment phases (pilot 3 months, ramp 6 months, steady state 12 months) with SKU mixes for each. We'll include explicit fallback lanes (same-family SKUs + cross-region fallback) and a cost-comparison table (hosted vs committed).

I attached a first-pass workbook (novacorp_rfi_answer_matrix_v1.xlsx) and a schematic of SKU-fit lanes. If that approach works I'll finalize numbers and send by EOD Friday.

Best,

Kim / Ben —

Looping in our sizing notes inline against Anya's sheet. Quick recommendations below (I quoted Kimberly's note for context):

> Plan: we'll draft a workbook that includes three commitment phases (pilot 3 months, ramp 6 months, steady state 12 months) with SKU mixes for each. We'll include explicit fallback lanes (same-family SKUs + cross-region fallback) and a cost-comparison table (hosted vs committed).

Sizing recommendations (short):
- Pilot (3 months): 4 x A10G (or equivalent) + 1 x A100-80GB mixed node for peak tests. Purpose: validate prefix caching and warm KV-hit rates. Budget headroom: +20% burst.
- Ramp (months 4–9): move to a 60/40 mix of A100-80GB to A10G for throughput-focused batch and cost-sensitive interactive. Reserve 10% of capacity as warm standby (fallback lane).
- Steady (12+ months): recommend shifting 70% to A100-80GB family (or latest Ampere-class), keep 30% on higher-density A10G for embeddings. For strict tail-latency p99 <= 350ms, maintain 15% dedicated low-latency pool (smaller sequence-length optimized kernels).

Quantization: For embeddings and rerank we can recommend 4-bit quantized variants yielding ~2.2x cost reduction with minimal QoE delta. For finance/PII-sensitive workloads, keep FP16; propose a hybrid policy per workload label.

Fallback lanes: prefer same-family fallback first (A100-80->A100-40), then cross-family with performance multiplier in workbook. Include region fallback (us-west -> us-east) with warm-state replication for user-sensitive flows.

I'll fill the numeric throughput rows in the workbook tonight (tokens/sec per GPU, concurrency assumptions, expected p95/p99) and return to Kimberly to finalize.

—Karthik

Subject: Final: Novacorp dedicated sizing workbook + next steps

Anya / Liam —

Attached is our completed sizing workbook (novacorp_rfi_answer_matrix_v1.xlsx) and a short schematic of SKU fitment and fallback lanes (sku-fitment-diagram.png). Summary highlights: 

- Pilot (0–3 months): 4 A10G + 1 A100-80GB. Estimated pilot throughput: interactive 8k tokens/sec aggregate (p95 ~110ms, p99 ~300ms); batch embeddings peak 120k embeddings/hour.
- Ramp (4–9 months): 6 A100-80GB + 8 A10G (60/40 split). Add 10% warm standby for sudden QPS spikes. Expected cost delta vs hosted: ~40% savings at steady-state.
- Steady (12+ months): 12 A100-80GB + 6 A10G with a 15% low-latency pool for strict p99 SLOs. With 4-bit quantization applied to embeddings/rerank we model a 2.0x–2.4x token-cost reduction; we flagged workload-by-workload recommendations in the workbook.
- Commitments & terms: standard 12-month reserved pool with quarterly usage reconciliation. We include term-sheet draft (reserved-commitment-term-sheet_draft.pdf) showing overage pricing and early-exit carveouts for M&A or regulatory reasons.

Assumptions we used (explicit in workbook): seq-length distributions (median/90/99), KV cache hit rates (pilot 30% -> steady 65%), and acceptable p95/p99 values you may change. If any of these differ we will rerun numbers.

Next steps: Can we schedule a 45-min engineering walkthrough on Monday 2nd at 10am PT to go through the workbook and decide pilot SKUs? We can also produce a tight DocuSign term-sheet after the call.

Thanks — looking forward.
